newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong high rise inferno claims 29 lives.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong high rise inferno claims 29 lives.

text.p: Twenty-nine people died and scores were injured as one of Hong Kong's worst fires in years tore through a commercial high rise and raged through the night, a government spokesman said on Thursday.
About 200 firefighters equipped with breathing apparatus and 38 fire trucks battled the blaze on Thursday morning, more than 14 hours after the fire broke out.
Flames and heavy smoke hampered efforts to search the ageing 16-storey building.
"Since the old building does not have modern fire protection facilities, rescue operation is particularly difficult," said Peter Cheung, the director of fire services.
Firefighters plucked more than 90 survivors from the building, a warren of small offices and workshops, to safety.
The fire broke out on Wednesday evening and quickly engulfed the bottom four storeys of the building.
It engulfed the top three floors after spreading upwards through the elevator shaft.

The blaze, believed to have been caused by a fault in an elevator, sent up flames and spewed a dark cloud over the Kowloon peninsula, blanking out the vision of helicopter pilots called in to winch up terrified survivors from the upper floors.
Others jumped from window ledges onto rescue ladders and some scrambled on to ledges and air conditioners, watched helplessly by friends and relatives in the crowded street below.
One of the dead was a fireman killed while battling the blaze. Liu Chi-ho, 40, is believed to have plunged down a lift shaft.
The government spokesman said 17 charred bodied were found on the 15th floor of the building in Nathan Road in the heart of the bustling Kowloon tourist district.

One man fell from the building in a rush to escape. Witnesses said they saw him climb from the window and cling to an air conditioner which gave way, sending the man plunging onto a canopy many storeys below.
A woman working in a shop that sells paintings in the building said that when she first smelled the fire she thought it was just the whiff of chemicals from a film laboratory next door.
